title: Normalization and data integrity

spans.alt: Relate tables with keys; parameterize queries
spans.caption: Relate tables with keys; parameterize queries

spans.text: “Normalization and data integrity” is a tool for solving a concrete programming problem. Identify the input and desired result, then trace what role the construct plays in the example. Study it not only as syntax, but also for its effects on readability, correctness, resource use, and future changes.
QUESTION: What will this example do? Predict the result first.
A course title is stored once in courses; enrollments refer to it through keys.

Normalization reduces repeated facts and helps prevent update anomalies. 1NF uses atomic column values and identifiable rows; 2NF removes dependencies on only part of a composite key; 3NF reduces dependencies between non-key columns. Start by identifying real functional dependencies.

Key line: `CREATE TABLE courses (`
What it does: A course title is stored once in courses; enrollments refer to it through keys.
Why it is used: When a fact is repeated, ask which copies must be updated when it changes.
If omitted or changed: Denormalization can be intentional for read performance, but then duplicated facts must be kept consistent.

spans.title: Common mistake
spans.text: Apply normalization to real dependencies rather than mechanically; excessive normalization can complicate queries.
